\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{−1,1\}^n\to\mathbb{R}$.
Then the noise stability of $f$ at correlation $\rho$ is
$\displaystyle\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}\rho^{|S|}\widehat f(S)^2$, where $\widehat
f(S)$ is the Fourier coefficient of $f$ at $S$.
\end{theorem}

\proofstep
  {FABL.noiseStability_eq_sum_rho_pow_mul_sq_fourierCoeff}
  {direct}
  {Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}
  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p056-b002,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p056-b003}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\rho\in[-1,1]$, and let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\mathbb
R$. Choose $x$ uniformly from the sign cube, then obtain $y$ by independently keeping
each coordinate of $x$ with probability $(1+\rho)/2$ and flipping it otherwise. The
expected product $\mathbb E[f(x)f(y)]$ equals
$\displaystyle\sum_{k=0}^{n}\rho^k\sum_{\begin{subarray}{c}S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\|S|=k\end{subarray}}\widehat
f(S)^2$, where $\widehat f(S)=\mathbb E_x\!\left[f(x)\prod_{i\in S}x_i\right]$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every $\rho\in[-1,1]$ and every Boolean function $f$, the noise stability of its
real-valued sign interpretation equals the expected value of $\rho^{|S|}$ when $S$ is
drawn from the spectral sample of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Total Fourier weight by levels]
\lean{FABL.sum_fourierWeightAtLevel_range}
\label{FABL.sum_fourierWeightAtLevel_range}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel}
\difficulty{4}
For every function $f$ from the sign cube $\{-1,1\}^n$ to $\mathbb R$, the sum of its
Fourier weights over levels $0$ through $n$ equals the sum of the squared Fourier
coefficients over all subsets of $\{1,\ldots,n\}$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise sensitivity by Fourier level]
\lean{FABL.noiseSensitivity_eq_sum_level}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p056-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p237-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p054-b002
}
\label{FABL.noiseSensitivity_eq_sum_level}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.noiseSensitivity_eq_half_sub_half_noiseStability, FABL.noiseStability_eq_sum_level_rho_pow_mul_fourierWeight, FABL.sum_fourierWeightAtLevel_range, FABL.sum_sq_fourierCoeff_eq_one}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\delta\le1$, and let $f$ map the $n$-dimensional
sign cube to signs. Its noise sensitivity at rate $\delta$ equals one half times the
sum, over levels $k=0,\ldots,n$, of $\bigl(1-(1-2\delta)^k\bigr)$ times the total
squared Fourier weight of the real-valued version of $f$ at level $k$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Noise sensitivity and total influence]
\lean{FABL.noiseSensitivity_le_delta_mul_totalInfluence}
\label{FABL.noiseSensitivity_le_delta_mul_totalInfluence}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction, FABL.BooleanFunction.toReal, FABL.fourierWeight, FABL.fourierWeightAtLevel, FABL.noiseSensitivity, FABL.noiseSensitivity_eq_sum_level, FABL.totalInfluence, FABL.totalInfluence_eq_sum_level_mul_fourierWeight}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f:\{-1,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and let
$0\leq\delta\leq1$. Choose $X$ uniformly from the sign cube and obtain $Y$ by
independently, in each coordinate, keeping the sign of $X$ with probability $1-\delta$
and flipping it with probability $\delta$. The probability that $f(X)\neq f(Y)$ is at
most $\delta$ times the total influence of $f$, where the influence in each coordinate
is the uniform expectation of the squared discrete derivative of $f$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For any two sets of coordinates $S,T$ in a finite sign cube, the Fourier coefficient at
$T$ of the monomial $x\mapsto\prod_{i\in S}x_i$ is $1$ if $S=T$ and $0$ otherwise.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
For every nonnegative integer $n$ and every $\rho\in[-1,1]$, the noise stability of the
constant function $1$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube is equal to $1$.
\end{theorem}

  {pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b004,
    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p053-b005}
\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $-1\leq\rho\leq1$, and let $f$ be the constant
function equal to $-1$ on the $n$-dimensional sign cube. Its noise stability at
correlation $\rho$—the expectation of $f(X)f(Y)$ when $(X,Y)$ is a $\rho$-correlated pair with the
correlated sign distribution—is $1$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{definition}[Parity function]
\lean{FABL.parityFunction}
\statementsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p023-b001,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p044-b002,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p148-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p209-b005
}
\label{FABL.parityFunction}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.BooleanFunction}
For a finite set $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, the parity function on sign vectors
$x\in\{-1,1\}^n$ is $\prod_{i\in S}x_i$, with values in the signs $\{-1,1\}$.
\end{definition}

\difficulty{3}
For every natural number $n$ and every subset $S$ of the $n$ coordinates, the
real-valued version of the parity function on $S$ is the monomial obtained by
multiplying the input signs indexed by $S$.
\end{theorem}

    pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p022-b004}
\difficulty{1}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and let
$0\leq\delta\leq1$. Define the parity function by $f(x)=\prod_{i\in S}x_i$. If each
coordinate of a uniformly chosen input is independently flipped with probability
$\delta$, then the probability that the parity changes is
$\frac{1-(1-2\delta)^{|S|}}{2}$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{3}
Let $n$ be a natural number, let $0\le\delta\le1$, and choose a coordinate $i$ among the
$n$ coordinates. The noise sensitivity at rate $\delta$ of the Boolean function that
returns coordinate $i$ is $\delta$.
\end{theorem}
